FN-X45DEE7-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 83
Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund Sponsor: Senator Rodger Smitherman
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 02/13/2024
Senate Bill 83 as introduced revises the amount and the cap that certain indigent defense
attorneys are paid based on the level of the original criminal charge as indicated below.
According to the Office of Indigent Services (OIDS), this will increase the obligations of the
Fair Trial Tax Fund, paid by the State General Fund, by an estimated $8.2 million dollars per
year.
Case Type Old Fee New Fee Old Cap New Cap
Capital Offense $70/Hr $120/Hr No Cap No Cap
Class A felony $70/HR $110/HR $4,000 $7,000
Class B felony $70/HR $90/HR $3,000 $6,000
Class C/D felony $70/HR $70/HR $2,000 $4,500
Juvenile $70/HR $80/HR $2,500 $4,500
Traffic $70/HR $55/HR N/A $1,500
Other $70/HR $70/HR $1,500 $2,500
Appeals $70/HR $85/HR $2,500 $5,000
Supreme Court $70/HR $85/HR $2,500 $5,000
In addition, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of OIDS and the indigent
defense advisory boards, by an undetermined amount, to comply with the provisions of this bill.

FN-X45DEE7-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 83
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Rodger Smitherman
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 03/04/2024
Senate Bill 83 as reported by the Committee on Judiciary would increase the obligations of the
Fair Trial Tax Fund, paid from the State General Fund, by an estimated $5.0 million dollars
annually, according to the Office of Indigent Services (OIDS), beginning in Fiscal Year 2025, by
revising the fee amounts paid to certain indigent defense attorneys, as follows:
Case Type Old Fee New Fee Old Cap New Cap
Capital Offense $70/Hr $120/Hr No Cap No Cap
Class A felony $70/HR $100/HR $4,000 $6,000
Class B felony $70/HR $80/HR $3,000 $4,000
Class C/D felony $70/HR $80/HR $2,000 $3,500
Juvenile $70/HR $70/HR $2,500 $4,500
Other $70/HR $55/HR $1,500 $2,000
Appeals $70/HR $85/HR $2,500 $5,000
Supreme Court $70/HR $85/HR $2,500 $5,000
In addition, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of OIDS and the indigent
defense advisory boards by an undetermined amount to comply with the provisions of this bill.

FN-X45DEE7-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 83
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Rodger Smitherman
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 02/28/2024
Senate Bill 83 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of the Fair Trial Tax Fund,
paid from the State General Fund, by an estimated $8.2 million dollars annually, according to
the Office of Indigent Services (OIDS), beginning in Fiscal Year 2025, by revising the fee
amounts paid to certain indigent defense attorneys, as follows:
Case Type Old Fee New Fee Old Cap New Cap
Capital Offense $70/Hr $120/Hr No Cap No Cap
Class A felony $70/HR $110/HR $4,000 $6,500
Class B felony $70/HR $90/HR $3,000 $6,000
Class C/D felony $70/HR $70/HR $2,000 $4,500
Juvenile $70/HR $80/HR $2,500 $4,500
Traffic $70/HR $55/HR N/A $1,500
Other $70/HR $70/HR $1,500 $2,500
Appeals $70/HR $85/HR $2,500 $5,000
Supreme Court $70/HR $85/HR $2,500 $5,000
In addition, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of OIDS and the indigent
defense advisory boards by an undetermined amount to comply with the provisions of this bill.
Finally, this bill would increase the obligations of the State General Fund, by a significant
undetermined amount, to provide reimbursement for indigent health care services provided in
the state at the Medicare reimbursement rate.
